proof_boundary: Explains local filesystem publication semantics and report readiness; it does not prove cloud object-store atomicity.
question: What prevents a half-written anonymized corpus from looking ready?
related_questions: What happens if the process crashes mid-publish?
Why is report.json the readiness marker?

bullets: Delete existing report.json before corpus mutation.
Fsync the output directory after removal.
steps.source_explanation: _publish unlinks report_path and fsyncs output_root before touching corpus.
steps.spoken: Readiness is invalidated first: _publish deletes any old report.json before it touches the corpus, then fsyncs the output directory. If the process dies after that point, readers do not see a stale success marker over changing bytes.
steps.title: Invalidate stale readiness

bullets: Recompute the staged corpus digest.
Mismatch rejects at SOURCE_CHANGED terminal.
Only a match can flow to corpus promotion.
steps.proof_boundary: Detects staging mutation, not undeclared sensitive data.
steps.source_explanation: _manifest_digest(staging / "corpus") must still match sealed_digest or _publish rejects.
steps.spoken: Before anything is promoted, _publish recomputes the staged corpus digest and compares it with sealed_digest. A mismatch raises SOURCE_CHANGED and ends in rejection; only a matching digest can continue to promote the corpus.
steps.title: Decide seal match before promotion

bullets: Only the seal-match branch reaches promotion.
Replace corpus before report.json exists.
Fsync the output directory after promotion.
steps.source_explanation: _publish replaces staging/corpus into output/corpus before creating the readiness marker.
steps.spoken: Only after stale readiness is gone and the seal decision matches does _publish promote the corpus. The mismatch branch has already ended in rejection, and the output directory is fsynced before the report marker is created.
steps.title: Promote corpus before marker

bullets: Write report bytes to .report.json.tmp.
Fsync the temporary report file before rename.
steps.source_explanation: _publish writes the JSON report to tmp and fsyncs the file descriptor.
steps.spoken: The report is first written to .report.json.tmp. _publish writes all bytes in a loop and fsyncs the temporary report before it can become report.json.
steps.title: Write and fsync temporary report

bullets: Atomically rename temp report to report.json.
Fsync the output directory after the final rename.
steps.source_explanation: _publish os.replace()s the temp report to report.json and then fsyncs output_root.
steps.spoken: The readiness marker appears last: _publish atomically renames the fsynced temp file to report.json, then fsyncs the output directory so the final rename is durable.
steps.title: Rename report.json last, then fsync directory

teleprompter_points: report.json is deleted before the corpus is touched, so stale readiness is invalidated first.
The staged corpus digest is an explicit decision: mismatch rejects at SOURCE_CHANGED, and only a match reaches promotion.
The corpus is promoted before the report marker.
report.json is written to a temporary file, fsynced, then atomically renamed last.
The output directory is fsynced after the final rename.
title: Fail-closed atomic publication writes report.json last

proof_boundary: Explains declared literal replacement behavior; it does not prove discovery of unlisted sensitive data.
question: How does the anonymizer avoid replacement cascades and overlap ambiguity?

bullets: Scan case-sensitive rules over original text.
Scan case-insensitive rules over ASCII-lowered text.
steps.proof_boundary: Policy validation owns rule safety before matching.
steps.source_explanation: Matcher.find merges raw spans from both automata.
steps.spoken: The matcher first scans the original text and its ASCII-lowered view, collecting candidate spans without changing the string. That means replacements cannot create new matches or hide later matches while scanning.
steps.title: Collect candidate spans

bullets: Sort by start, longest span, then rule_id.
Skip spans overlapping an already-selected range.
steps.proof_boundary: Runtime selection is deterministic for validated policies.
steps.spoken: Overlap ambiguity is resolved in _select: candidates sort by earliest start, then longest span, then rule id, and anything overlapping an accepted span is skipped. Matcher.replace then rebuilds the output once from that fixed plan, so emitted pseudonyms are never rescanned.
steps.title: Pick non-overlapping spans

teleprompter_points: The matcher scans original text with Aho-Corasick automata.
Case-insensitive matching uses an ASCII-lowered length-preserving view.
Candidates are selected leftmost-longest with rule_id tie-break.
Replacement is a single pass and never rescans emitted pseudonyms.
title: Deterministic literal matching resolves overlaps once

proof_boundary: Explains the local report contract and explicit non-claims; it does not requalify the frozen runtime archive.
question: What does the trial report prove, and what does it deliberately not claim?
related_questions: Why are non-claims in the report?
How does the report bind source and output bytes?

bullets: Store policy/source/verification digests.
Keep counts and algorithm identifiers in one schema.
steps.proof_boundary: Hash binding only covers declared pipeline inputs and outputs.
steps.source_explanation: RunReport carries hashes and counts for the final readiness marker.
steps.spoken: RunReport is the readiness contract: it records counts, policy hash, source manifest hash, verification hash, and the verified corpus digest. That binds report.json to the exact inputs and staged bytes this run checked.
steps.title: Bind report to inputs and verified output

bullets: List discovery and linkage limits in does_not_establish.
Prevent green report from implying formal anonymity.
steps.proof_boundary: Bounded trial claim, not formal privacy guarantee.
steps.spoken: The report also states what it does not prove: discovery of unlisted sensitive data, external-linkage resistance, quasi-identifier anonymity, or differential privacy. Those non-claims prevent a green report from being oversold.
steps.title: Say what is not established

teleprompter_points: RunReport binds status, counts, policy hash, source manifest hash, and verification hash.
does_not_establish lists non-claims such as quasi-identifier anonymity and differential privacy.
The report is readiness evidence for this literal-policy pipeline, not a universal anonymization proof.
title: Run report states proof boundaries explicitly

proof_boundary: Explains the value-scoped transform and verification code paths for covered JSON/SQLite/CSV/TXT representations; it does not by itself provide live runtime proof, external re-identification resistance, or differential privacy.
question: How did you fix the typed-PII disqualifier, and how do you know the same class of miss can't recur?
related_questions: Why did the original submission miss integer-typed phone numbers?
How is the check derived from the delivered spec instead of the code?

bullets: A phone stored as an integer is the same phone.
Numeric tokens are matched against policy values.
A matching numeric scalar is replaced with the pseudonym string.
steps.proof_boundary: Covers JSON string/int/float and SQLite TEXT/INTEGER/REAL; BLOB fails closed elsewhere.
steps.source_explanation: _replace_json stringifies numeric scalars with _numeric_tokens before matching policy values.
steps.spoken: The transform fix is value-scoped: a sensitive number is treated as the same value as its text spelling. In _replace_json, numeric scalar tokens are matched against the policy and a matching scalar is replaced with its pseudonym string.
steps.title: Match the value, not the spelling

bullets: Reload released files through decoded searchable surfaces.
Include JSON scalar tokens, SQLite DDL, raw bytes, headers, tables, and views.
steps.proof_boundary: Enumerates supported searchable surfaces; it is not a measured claim about unsupported formats.
steps.source_explanation: iter_searchable_text yields decoded JSON/CSV/TXT text plus SQLite raw bytes, schema fields, header integers, table cells, and view cells.
steps.spoken: The verifier gets its own searchable view of the released output. iter_searchable_text reloads supported files and yields JSON scalar text, CSV/TXT text, SQLite raw bytes, schema text, header integers, base table cells, and view cells.
steps.title: Search every covered surface

bullets: Normalize both probe and output text to NFC.
Count policy literals without reusing the transform matcher.
steps.proof_boundary: Literal absence over searchable surfaces, not formal anonymity.
steps.source_explanation: _count independently NFC-normalizes and counts protected values in source and output searchable text.
steps.spoken: The absence oracle is a separate count over searchable text. _count normalizes both the policy value and output text to NFC and counts occurrences without going through the transform matcher.
steps.title: Count normalized absences independently

bullets: Read sensitive values from policy.json.
Scan the released corpus for those values.
Report leaks instead of accepting a code-shaped list.
steps.proof_boundary: The script derives values from policy.json; this explainer does not claim a live run receipt.
steps.source_explanation: spec_derived_check.py reads policy.json, decodes corpus scalars, and reports any surviving policy value.
steps.spoken: The release gate is spec-derived: spec_derived_check.py reads values from policy.json and scans the corpus for those values. That keeps the check anchored to the delivered policy instead of a hand-authored list copied from the implementation.
steps.title: The check comes from the spec, not the code

teleprompter_points: The disqualifier: a phone stored as a JSON/SQLite integer passed the original string-only path.
The transform now treats matching numeric scalar values as sensitive values, not just sensitive spellings.
The verifier scans decoded JSON/SQLite surfaces, schema text, raw SQLite bytes, header integers, views, and normalized counts.
The release gate is spec-derived: it reads policy.json values instead of a hardcoded value list.
title: Value-scoped anonymization and representation hardening

proof_boundary: Explains the local single-process anonymization trial path from bundle intake to ready report; it does not claim differential privacy, external re-identification resistance, or distributed storage semantics.
question: Walk me through your solution from receiving an input dataset to releasing the anonymized result.
related_questions: How does the input dataset become the anonymized output?
What happens between policy.json intake and report.json release?
Walk me through the anonymization pipeline end to end.

bullets: Require a regular policy.json and corpus/ directory.
Reject unsafe or unsupported input before staging.
Record source digests before transformation.
steps.proof_boundary: Preflight covers declared local files and policy rules, not discovery of undeclared sensitive data.
steps.source_explanation: run_pipeline loads policy.json, validates the corpus tree, inventories source digests, and creates a private staging directory before any output is marked ready.
steps.spoken: The walkthrough starts at preflight: policy.json and corpus/ must be ordinary inputs, roots cannot be nested, every corpus entry must be a regular supported file, and sensitive literals in paths are rejected before staging.
steps.title: Receive and preflight the dataset

bullets: Write anonymized files into private staging.
Replace policy values across supported scalar representations.
Keep unfinished output away from the readiness marker.
steps.proof_boundary: Transforms values covered by the delivered policy and supported formats.
steps.source_explanation: transform_file and the format-specific replacers write anonymized records into the staging corpus, including scalar value handling for JSON and SQLite surfaces.
steps.spoken: Next, run_pipeline writes transformed files into a private staging corpus. The output is not ready during this phase because report.json has not been published.
steps.title: Transform into a staged anonymized corpus

bullets: Run an independent verifier over staged output.
Reject if source files changed during processing.
Hash the verified staged corpus before publish.
steps.proof_boundary: The seal proves the verified staged bytes are the bytes sent to publish.
steps.source_explanation: After verify_corpus passes, run_pipeline rejects source drift, computes sealed_digest over the staged corpus, and passes that digest into _publish.
steps.spoken: Then verification runs on the staged corpus, the source files are rehashed to catch drift, and the verified staged bytes are sealed with a manifest digest.
steps.title: Verify and seal what will be released

bullets: Remove stale report.json before changing output.
Recheck the sealed digest immediately before publish.
Write report.json last as the only ready signal.
steps.source_explanation: _publish removes stale report.json, rechecks sealed_digest, swaps corpus into place, and atomically writes report.json last as the readiness marker.
steps.spoken: Finally _publish removes stale readiness, rechecks the sealed digest, promotes the corpus, fsyncs it, writes and fsyncs the temporary report, and renames report.json last as the ready signal.
steps.title: Publish corpus first, report.json last

teleprompter_points: The input bundle is accepted only after policy.json and corpus/ pass preflight.
Each supported file is transformed into a private staging corpus.
Verification scans the staged corpus against the policy-derived sensitive values.
The verified corpus is sealed, published, and only then report.json marks the release ready.
title: Input dataset to ready anonymized release
